process_nodes.label: 180 nm and above
process_nodes.note: The trade report puts the expansion on 180 nm and larger processes; the CHIPS project page names 180 nm and 350 nm.

summary: Analog Devices plans to spend more than USD 1 billion expanding its Beaverton, Oregon wafer fab, which trade press described as its largest fab by volume. The plan grows cleanroom space by about 25,000 sq ft to roughly 118,000 sq ft and nearly doubles internal output on 180 nm and larger processes. Oregon finalized a USD 12 million state grant for the expansion in June 2024, and in January 2025 the federal CHIPS program signed preliminary terms for up to USD 105 million shared with ADI projects in Camas, Washington and Chelmsford, Massachusetts.

notes: The federal CHIPS release also targets about 70% more capacity across the Beaverton and Camas fabs. ADI's FY2025 annual report lists Beaverton as an owned wafer fabrication site of about 458,000 sq ft but does not report on the expansion. No source read here dates construction or completion, and no final federal award notice was found.
